description.narrative: The project is implemented in Turkey. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy and human rights and gender equality. The main right holders are youth within the Roma community in Turkey. Through campaigning, trainings, organising and capacity building and the establishment of a popular education programme called The Other School of Politics the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between the local partner organisation Zero Discrimination Association and The Workers Educational Association (ABF-förbundet). The local partner organisation Zero Discrimination Association works for antidiscrimination of the Roma people and its activities aim to include the Roma youth in the Turkish society and ensure their active participation in the political arena in Turkey. The ABF, one of the Palme Center's member organisations, is highly engaged in the development in Turkey, with a member base interested in contributing to the democratic development of the country. They support this partnership with their specific focus on and expertise in people's education. The Palme Center will support the project with administrative and technical support.Other Donors to the OrganisationOther donors to the organisation are among others the Council of Europe in Strasbourg. The relationship between the Council of Europe and the Palme Center can be further developed, both regarding donor coordination, but also for other synergies regarding the council's work with the Roma community in Europe. The Council of Europe has during the past years raised its interest in meeting with the labour movement in Sweden, which needs to be further followed up by the Palme Center's leadership.Other donors to the organisation are the Dutch Consulate, Swiss Consulate, Open Society Foundations, European Commission, and CFCU (Central Finance and Contracts Unit).Project ObjectiveThe overall objective is to ensure the active participation (in social, political and economic life) of young Roma people who cannot access fundamental rights and therefore cannot participate actively in politics. The project aims to strengthen social integration of the Roma. The intermediate objectives of the project are:- Informing the Roma youth about human rights, democracy, gender equality, equal citizenship and increase the knowledge of the target group through training modules. - Monitoring and teaching social policy implementation - Establishing collaborations within the target group ensured by a common online learning platform. - Strengthening the social and rights-based project development and implementation capacities of young people through seed funding.- Sharing the qualified learning material and research with all segments of the society and thus supporting social integration processes.Actor groupsThe organisation's main actors within the different actors groups are: 1) right holders: Roma youth and other marginalized minorities and people such as women and LGBTQI.2) actors working in cooperation: universities, national and international NGOs and human rights activists working on human rights, anti-discrimination and other actors such as the Council of Europe, EU, Swedish MEPs.3) decision makers (in Turkey): the different government agencies working on human rights, labour rights and minority rights, such as the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Labour and Social Security, UN, European Union and Council of Europe.
